pathway.title: Routine Prenatal Care
pathway.scope: Outpatient antepartum care for every pregnancy under supervision, from the first prenatal contact to birth: intake and dating, the initial laboratory panel, genetic screening options, psychosocial screening, preeclampsia risk and aspirin, supplements, immunizations and counselling, every-visit monitoring, and gestational-age-windowed care including gestational diabetes screening and diagnosis. Screens for diabetes, hypertension, anemia and Rh(D)-negative blood type and recommends adding the diagnosis; treatment of each belongs to its own pathway.
pathway.target_population: Pregnant patients receiving outpatient prenatal care, average risk or under high-risk supervision.

properties.title: Initial prenatal assessment and whole-pregnancy care
properties.description: Dating, history and risk, the initial laboratory panel (each test ordered only when it is not already on file), psychosocial screening, genetic screening options, preeclampsia risk and aspirin, supplements, counselling and immunizations given at any gestational age.

properties.title: Confirm pregnancy and establish gestational age and due date
properties.description: Assign the due date as soon as the last menstrual period and/or first ultrasound are available. First-trimester ultrasound (crown-rump length, up to 13 6/7 weeks) is the most accurate method (plus or minus 5-7 days). Redate to ultrasound when it differs from menstrual dating by more than: 5 days up to 8 6/7 weeks; 7 days at 9 0/7-15 6/7 weeks; 10 days at 16 0/7-21 6/7 weeks; 14 days at 22 0/7-27 6/7 weeks; 21 days from 28 weeks (with caution). A pregnancy with no ultrasound confirming or revising the due date before 22 0/7 weeks is suboptimally dated. Assisted-reproduction pregnancies use the ART-derived due date. Record gestational age in completed weeks: every time-windowed part of this pathway reads it.
Encounter for supervision of normal first pregnancy, unspecified trimester

properties.name: HEDIS Prenatal and Postpartum Care (PPC): Timeliness of Prenatal Care
properties.measure: Denominator: deliveries of live births between October 8 of the prior year and October 7 of the measurement year. Numerator: a prenatal visit in the first trimester, on or before the enrollment start date, or within 42 days of enrollment. Steward: NCQA; also CMS Maternity Core Set PPC2-CH / PPC2-AD.

properties.title: Comprehensive history, risk assessment and physical examination
properties.description: History: obstetric and gynecologic (prior pregnancies and outcomes, menstrual history, infertility or ART, cervical screening, sexual and STI history, teratogen exposures); medical (chronic conditions, mental health, substance use, eating disorders, surgeries, medications and supplements, immunizations, oral health); family and genetic history; social drivers of health. Exam: blood pressure, height, weight and BMI. Classify as average or greater-than-average risk to tailor the visit schedule. High-risk findings are noted here and managed outside this pathway: multifetal gestation; prior spontaneous preterm birth (cervical length surveillance); prior cesarean (TOLAC counselling); age 35 or older; BMI 30 or higher; opioid use disorder.

properties.title: Initial prenatal laboratory panel: what is already on file
properties.description: The chart is read test by test. A test already resulted is not ordered again: blood type and Rh, the hemoglobinopathy evaluation and the hepatitis B triple panel count if ever resulted; every other test counts if drawn this pregnancy. The most recent hemoglobin and the Rh(D) type are read here: a low hemoglobin or an Rh(D)-negative type opens a step recommending that the diagnosis be added, and treatment then belongs to that problem's own pathway. Weak D (Du-positive) patients are not at risk of alloimmunization. TB testing and TSH only if at risk; cervical cancer screening on the routine schedule.

properties.title: Low hemoglobin: add the anemia diagnosis
properties.description: The most recent hemoglobin is below the trimester threshold: under 11.0 g/dL in the first or third trimester, under 10.5 g/dL in the second. The anemia in pregnancy pathway then applies and owns the workup and treatment; this pathway orders none of it.

properties.title: Rh(D)-negative: add the diagnosis
properties.description: The Rh(D) type is negative and no Rh-negative blood type is on the problem list. Record it: Z67.91 (unspecified blood type, Rh negative) or the ABO-specific code (Z67.11, Z67.21, Z67.31, Z67.41). Rh-negative management, including Rh immune globulin, belongs to its own pathway; routine prenatal care types the blood and runs the antibody screen only. A positive antibody screen (alloimmunization) is O36.01- and needs maternal-fetal medicine.

properties.topic: Rh(D)-negative: what routine care does not cover

Psychosocial and behavioral screening
properties.description: Depression and anxiety: a validated instrument (EPDS or PHQ-9; GAD-7) at the initial visit, again later in pregnancy and postpartum; assess suicide risk the same day if a self-harm item is positive. Refer patients at increased risk of perinatal depression to counselling (CBT or IPT). Intimate partner violence: screen privately at the first visit and each trimester. Substance use: screen everyone with a validated interview tool; biologic testing is not a screening tool and needs consent. Tobacco, nicotine and alcohol: ask, advise, intervene. Social drivers of health: a standardized tool at intake; refer or coordinate.

properties.name: HEDIS Prenatal Depression Screening and Follow-Up (PND-E)
properties.measure: Screening: a standardized instrument between the start of pregnancy and delivery. Follow-up: within 30 days of a positive screen. Steward: NCQA (ECDS).

properties.title: Genetic screening and diagnostic testing options
properties.description: Make cell-free DNA screening for trisomies 21, 18 and 13 routinely available to all, at any gestational age from 9-10 weeks; every patient may pursue or decline. Serum screening is for patient preference or when cell-free DNA cannot be used. Diagnostic testing is available: chorionic villus sampling at 10-13 weeks, amniocentesis usually at 15-20 weeks. A positive or nonreportable result leads to genetic counselling, detailed ultrasound and diagnostic testing. Offer everyone cystic fibrosis and spinal muscular atrophy carrier screening (once per lifetime; a carrier leads to partner testing). Fragile X only with a family history or unexplained ovarian insufficiency.

properties.title: Preeclampsia risk assessment
properties.description: High-risk factors (any one): prior preeclampsia, multifetal gestation, chronic hypertension, pregestational diabetes, kidney disease, autoimmune disease such as lupus or antiphospholipid syndrome. Moderate-risk factors (more than one): nulliparity, BMI over 30, family history, Black race (a proxy for racism), lower income, age 35 or older, personal-history factors, in vitro conception. The medication list is read first: a patient already on low-dose aspirin is not asked about eligibility again.

Qualifies with ANY ONE high-risk factor (prior preeclampsia, multifetal gestation, chronic hypertension, pregestational type 1 or 2 diabetes, kidney disease, autoimmune disease such as SLE or antiphospholipid syndrome); OR TWO OR MORE moderate-risk factors (nulliparity, BMI >30, family history of preeclampsia in mother or sister, Black race, lower income, age 35 or older, personal history factors, in vitro conception); OR, on its own, Black race or lower income.

properties.title: Supplements and healthy-pregnancy counselling
properties.description: The medication list is read first: a folic acid supplement already on it is continued, not started again. After a prior pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect: folic acid 4 mg daily as a separate supplement through the first 3 months (CDC: start 1 month before conception; ACOG: at least 3 months before). Iron requirement 27 mg a day; choose a vitamin containing iodine (150 mcg a day as potassium iodide). Avoid NSAIDs from 20 weeks, except aspirin 81 mg.

properties.topic: Urgent maternal warning signs
properties.instructions: Review the urgent maternal warning signs (CDC Hear Her / AIM) with the patient and give her the handout; she should seek care immediately for any of them. The warning signs apply during pregnancy and for a year after birth. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/hearher/maternal-warning-signs/index.html

properties.topic: Pregnancy weight gain
properties.instructions: How much weight is healthy to gain depends on your weight before pregnancy. Underweight (BMI under 18.5): 28-40 pounds. Normal weight (18.5-24.9): 25-35 pounds. Overweight (25-29.9): 15-25 pounds. Obesity (30 or higher): 11-20 pounds. You don't need extra calories in the first trimester. Later you need only about 340 extra calories a day in the second trimester and about 450 in the third. We will check your weight at visits and can connect you with a nutrition or activity program.

properties.topic: Eating well and food safety in pregnancy
properties.instructions: To avoid listeria, a germ that can harm your baby: skip raw (unpasteurized) milk and cheeses made from it; heat deli meats and hot dogs until steaming hot; avoid refrigerated smoked fish, premade deli salads and raw sprouts. Eat 2 to 3 servings a week of low-mercury fish such as salmon, shrimp, cod or canned light tuna. Do not eat shark, swordfish, king mackerel, marlin, orange roughy, Gulf tilefish or bigeye tuna. Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day.

properties.topic: Alcohol, tobacco and cannabis in pregnancy
properties.instructions: No amount or type of alcohol is known to be safe at any time in pregnancy. If you drank before you knew you were pregnant, the most important thing is to stop now. Quitting smoking and other tobacco at any point helps you and your baby, and we can help you quit. There is no medical reason to use cannabis in pregnancy, and we advise stopping.

properties.topic: Staying active in pregnancy
properties.instructions: Aim for at least 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, such as brisk walking, swimming or stationary cycling. You should be able to talk while exercising. Avoid contact sports, activities where you might fall, scuba diving, and lying flat on your back for long periods later in pregnancy. Stop and call us if you have vaginal bleeding, belly pain, fluid leaking, painful regular contractions, chest pain, dizziness, headache, shortness of breath before exercising, calf pain or swelling, or weakness that affects your balance.

properties.topic: Dental care and travel in pregnancy
properties.instructions: Dental checkups, cleanings, X-rays with a shield and numbing medicine are all safe in pregnancy, and needed fillings or root canals can be done at any time. Always wear your seat belt, with the lap belt below your belly and the shoulder belt between your breasts. Occasional flights are usually fine in a healthy pregnancy. On long flights, get up and walk around from time to time, drink fluids, and consider support stockings.

properties.title: Immunizations at any gestational age
properties.description: Influenza vaccine in any trimester during the season (third-trimester patients as soon as vaccine is available; the live intranasal vaccine is contraindicated). COVID-19 vaccine per ACOG, with shared decision-making and the discussion documented. Hepatitis B vaccine if susceptible on the triple panel. MMR and varicella vaccines are contraindicated in pregnancy: give postpartum if non-immune. Immunization records are not read from the chart: confirm what has already been given this season and this pregnancy before ordering.

properties.name: Influenza vaccine, inactivated or recombinant
properties.instructions: Any trimester, during the season. The live intranasal vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy. May be given with Tdap, RSV and COVID-19 vaccines.

properties.description: Influenza virus vaccine, trivalent (IIV3), preservative free, 0.5 mL, intramuscular
Influenza virus vaccine, trivalent, recombinant (RIV3), intramuscular

properties.name: COVID-19 vaccine (current-season formulation)
properties.dose: one dose of the current-season product
properties.instructions: Recommended in any trimester per ACOG (Committee Statement No. 26, 2026: all pregnant and lactating individuals should receive an updated COVID-19 vaccine). Offer it through shared decision-making and document the discussion. CDC's current position differs: the CDC adult immunization schedule (Jul 2 2025) gives no guidance for pregnancy, and CDC's interim clinical considerations (updated Sep 23 2026) advise a review of the risks and benefits.

properties.title: Every prenatal visit
properties.description: Blood pressure with a hand-off for an elevated reading, weight, fetal heart and movement, fundal height, symptom review, and the tailored visit schedule.

properties.title: Blood pressure at every visit
properties.description: A positive screen is a systolic pressure of 140 mm Hg or higher or a diastolic of 90 or higher. Confirm with a repeat measurement; the diagnosis needs two readings at least 4 hours apart. Severe range is 160/110 or higher.

properties.title: Elevated blood pressure: confirm and add the diagnosis
properties.description: Severe range (160/110 or higher): same-day evaluation. At 20 weeks or later, record R03.0 (elevated blood-pressure reading without a diagnosis of hypertension) until confirmed, then O13.x (gestational hypertension) or O14.x (preeclampsia); the hypertension in pregnancy pathway then applies and owns the evaluation and treatment. Before 20 weeks, evaluate for chronic hypertension.
Elevated blood-pressure reading, without diagnosis of hypertension

properties.topic: Elevated blood pressure: what happens next
properties.instructions: Today's blood pressure is 140/90 or higher. Repeat it. If it stays elevated, add the diagnosis to the problem list (R03.0 until confirmed; gestational hypertension or preeclampsia once confirmed) so the hypertension in pregnancy pathway can guide the evaluation. Urine protein is tested only when preeclampsia is suspected, not routinely.

properties.title: Routine per-visit assessment
properties.description: Weight. Fetal heart activity at the appropriate gestational age. Fundal height at in-person visits from 24 weeks: a difference from gestational age of more than 3 cm warrants a growth ultrasound. Fetal movement after quickening. Symptoms: contractions, fluid leakage, bleeding. Home blood pressure and weight self-monitoring is acceptable when the patient is trained and equipped.

properties.title: Tailored visit schedule
properties.description: Average risk: intake plus about 8 visits. Greater-than-average risk: intake plus about 13 visits. Telehealth where no exam, laboratory test, imaging or vaccine is needed. Tailored care does not mean less care.

properties.interval: Tailored: intake plus about 8 visits (average risk) or about 13 (greater than average)
properties.description: Sample schedule: in person at about 10, 16, 28, 36 and 39 weeks; any modality at 22, 32 and 38 weeks; anatomy ultrasound at about 20 weeks. Traditional reference: every 4 weeks to 28, every 2 weeks to 36, then weekly.

properties.description: The most recent hemoglobin A1c decides: 6.5% or higher is diabetes; 5.9-6.4% is early abnormal glucose metabolism. The one-step and two-step gestational diabetes criteria are not applied before 24 weeks. Alternatives to the A1c, not ordered here: fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL or higher; 2-hour 75-g value 200 or higher; random 200 or higher with classic symptoms.

This is diabetes complicating pregnancy, not gestational diabetes: record O24.111 / O24.112 / O24.113 (pre-existing type 2 diabetes in pregnancy, by trimester), or O24.911-O24.919 if the type is unspecified. Management belongs to the diabetes problem, not to routine prenatal care.

properties.instructions: Your early A1C was slightly above normal. This means a higher chance of developing gestational diabetes later in pregnancy. We will meet with a dietitian and may check your fasting blood sugar a few times a week. Whether treating this early helps is still being studied; we will decide together.

properties.title: Gestational diabetes status: read from the chart
properties.description: A diabetes-in-pregnancy code on the problem list means already diagnosed: no screening. A screening result on file is read: a 50-g challenge below 140 mg/dL, or a 75-g test with all three values below threshold, means screening is complete. Otherwise screening is open. Universal screening is at 24 0/7 weeks or later; screen as soon as possible if first seen after 28 weeks. After bariatric surgery with dumping, a glucose load may not be tolerated: consider alternatives.

properties.description: The 50-g challenge on file is below 140 mg/dL, or all three 75-g values are below threshold (fasting 92, 1-hour 180, 2-hour 153 mg/dL). No repeat screening unless clinically suspected (new glycosuria, suspected macrosomia or polyhydramnios). A result drawn before 24 weeks does not count as the screen: order it if that is the case.

properties.topic: What a negative glucose screen settles
properties.instructions: The glucose screening result on file is negative, so gestational diabetes screening is complete and is not repeated. Retest only on clinical suspicion: new glycosuria, a fetus measuring large, or excess amniotic fluid. If the result on file was drawn before 24 weeks it is not the screen; order the screening test.

properties.title: Gestational diabetes screening is open: choose the strategy
properties.description: No diabetes diagnosis and no negative screen on file. Either strategy is acceptable: two-step (50-g 1-hour challenge, then a 100-g 3-hour test if it is 140 mg/dL or higher) or one-step (75-g 2-hour test). A 50-g result already on file means the two-step strategy is under way.

properties.topic: GDM screening: what the glucose test involves
properties.instructions: Every pregnant patient is checked for gestational diabetes between 24 and 28 weeks. In the two-step approach you drink a 50-gram glucose drink (no fasting needed) and have blood drawn one hour later. If that result is high, a second, longer test follows: after an overnight fast you drink 100 grams of glucose and have blood drawn fasting and at 1, 2 and 3 hours. In the one-step approach you fast overnight, drink 75 grams of glucose, and have blood drawn fasting and at 1 and 2 hours. Stay seated and do not eat or smoke during the test.

properties.topic: GDM diagnosis: what happens next
properties.instructions: Gestational diabetes means your body is not handling sugar as well as it needs to during pregnancy. Most patients (about 70-85%) control it with changes in eating and activity alone. We will refer you to a dietitian and teach you to check your blood sugar at home. Well-controlled gestational diabetes lowers the chance of a very large baby, birth injury and low blood sugar in your newborn.

properties.title: Repeat psychosocial screening and birth and postpartum planning
properties.description: Depression and anxiety screen later in pregnancy; intimate partner violence screen this trimester. Breastfeeding: intention, support and referral. Reproductive life plan and postpartum contraception: avoid interpregnancy intervals under 6 months and discuss the risks under 18 months; for Medicaid sterilization, consent must be signed at least 30 days before the procedure. Postpartum care plan: contact within 3 weeks, comprehensive visit by 12 weeks.

properties.topic: Your baby's movements
properties.instructions: Get to know your baby's usual pattern of movement. If your baby is moving less than usual or has stopped moving, call us the same day. Don't wait until the next day.

properties.topic: Breastfeeding and planning birth control
properties.instructions: Breastfeeding has health benefits for you and your baby. The choice is yours, and if you would like to breastfeed we can connect you with lactation support before and after birth. Let's also plan birth control for after delivery. Waiting 18 months or more before your next pregnancy lowers risks, and some methods can be started before you leave the hospital.

properties.name: HEDIS Prenatal and Postpartum Care (PPC): Postpartum Care
properties.measure: Numerator: a postpartum visit on or between 7 and 84 days after delivery. A planning metric here: the visit is scheduled during prenatal care. Steward: NCQA.

properties.topic: Signs of labor and timing of birth
properties.instructions: True labor contractions come regularly, get closer together, and don't go away with rest. Call us if you think you're in labor or your water breaks, and go to the hospital for heavy bleeding. If this is your first full-term pregnancy and you and your baby are healthy, we can talk about an induction at 39 weeks. If you haven't delivered by 41 weeks, we will check on your baby once or twice a week and plan delivery.
